ai_mode_switch_fix.cause: Mode buttons were disabled when audio was running.
ai_mode_switch_fix.behavior: Mode buttons remain enabled while running; selecting a different mode requests a muted worker stop, releases the settings, and retains the virtual microphone until resume or close. Clicking the same mode does not stop audio.
ai_mode_switch_fix.additional_assertions: Same virtual source index during pause and resume, failed API validation keeps that input connected, settings unlock, close cleans up, hardware defaults unchanged. Synthetic fixtures only.

prior_ai_tests: Real local STT/TTS and mocked API pipeline results are retained from 1.4.0. This Linux buffering fix reruns the native AI bridge and mode switching, not heavyweight model inference or live API.

game_audio_fix.scope: Linux PipeWire/PulseAudio only; Windows WASAPI unchanged and native binary rebuilt
game_audio_fix.cause: Ordinary-priority audio worker competing with games; playback safety reserve too short for long scheduling stalls; capture catch-up truncated by old 100 ms local queue limit.
changes: Request real-time audio worker priority 5 via libpulse, with per-thread nice -10 fallback if available. No privileged helper or game/server priority changes.
Both playback streams target 200 ms and prebuffer 160 ms, independent of hardware latency.
Drain up to 32 capture fragments per iteration and write each processed DSP block during catch-up.
Local queues bounded to 500 ms rather than discarding burst audio after 100 ms.
game_audio_fix.environment: CachyOS; THE FINALS process running during synthetic tests. Tests use isolated virtual input/output and synthetic tone; personal microphone not recorded.
game_audio_fix.tradeoff: Around 100 ms added to previous send safety reserve. End-to-end latency depends on devices, DSP, server and receiving application. Stalls beyond the reserve or physical microphone disconnects can still interrupt audio.
game_audio_fix.real_game_or_discord_call: Not verified; needs user confirmation with actual speech.
